subject: Post-demo: Trela POC scope, SDK auth, routing & prompt governance
messages:
From: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Rivera <alex.rivera@trela.ai>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-08-02T15:12:00-07:00
Subject: Recap + immediate asks from today's demo (SDK/auth/routing + prompt governance)

Hi Alex —

Thanks again for taking the call today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we keep momentum for a POC:

Key takeaways from our side:
- Primary goals: sub-250ms median inference on LLM-based summarization + context-aware reranking for search results.
- Data constraints: PII in some logs, must remain in Trela VPC; public models acceptable if run in private deployment.
- Success metric: 15%+ relevance lift on reranker + cost target under $0.003/token for batch-run flows.

Immediate asks / blockers:
1) Can you share an architecture diagram showing where the inference service will sit relative to your API gateway and embeddings store? (we referenced this on-screen)
2) Who owns auth/OIDC at Trela for issuing short-lived credentials for our Private deployment?
3) Security QA — you've got a couple items we flagged; if possible, please upload the security questionnaire and any SOC2 audit report.

From our technical side (we'll scope these into the M.A.P):
- SDK: we'll provide a lightweight SDK (node + python) with built-in retry/backoff and automatic prefix caching controls. Sample config attached.
- Auth: support for API keys and OIDC with short-lived tokens; we recommend OIDC for POC for better rotation and auditability.
- Routing: suggest a read-path to a cheaper hosted model for non-sensitive traffic, and a private-only route for PII paths.
- Structured output / tool-calling: plan to use function-calling for deterministic entity extraction and a schema-validated JSON response.
- Embeddings + reranker: we propose using a local FAISS store for embeddings during POC and a lightweight supervised reranker pair for final scoring.

Prompt governance items (high priority for Trela):
- We'll supply a prompt template repo with semantic versioning (v1.0, v1.1...) and immutable tags for production.
- System prompts will be stored separately from user prompts; we will sign and checksum system prompts to detect drift.
- We recommend an initial red-team pass focusing on prompt injection vectors on any user-supplied content.

Next steps / timeline proposal:
- Trela to share architecture diagram + security QA by EOD 8/3
- Redwood to deliver SDK samples + mutual action plan 8/4 (attached)
- Kickoff POC environment week of 8/10 pending approvals

I'll hold on scheduling the technical deep dive until we have the architecture diagram and auth contact. If that's all accurate, I'll convert this into the formal MAP and attach the config/examples.

Thanks —
Connor O'Brien
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
connor.obrien@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0192

Thanks Connor — good summary. A few quick clarifications: 

- Architecture diagram: attaching a rough internal diagram (see trela-arch-v1.pdf attached to this message). It shows our API gateway, internal event bus, embeddings store (managed ElasticSearch), and a separate analytics VPC. Our security team prefers traffic to go through the gateway for auditing.
- Auth: J. Patel (cc'd) owns OIDC and will coordinate issuing a test client.
- Security QA: attaching a low-sensitivity SOC snapshot and our answered questionnaire — some redacted fields for confidentiality.

On the prompt governance front — we like the idea of prompt template versioning. Our legal asks that system prompts are auditable and that there is an immutable history. We'll need any checksum/signing approach documented for compliance.

We can commit to sharing the full architecture and the security questionnaire by EOD 8/3. For the POC, we're comfortable with a private deployment with a route to hosted models for non-sensitive logs.

Alex

From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>

Subject: Internal: POC integration proposal for Trela (SDK/auth/routing, embeddings, prompt governance)

Folks —

I drafted a concise integration approach we can present in the technical deep dive once we receive Trela's diagram:

1) SDK / onboarding
- Ship node/python SDKs with an \"environment\" config block: {deployment: private|hosted, model_variant: name, prompt_version: tag}. SDK will support automatic token refresh (OIDC) and an api_key fallback.
- Samples: quickstart with function-calling enabled for entity extraction, and a second example showing structured-output schema validation.

2) Auth & routing
- Recommend OIDC for POC (client_credentials flow) with 10m short-lived tokens from Trela's identity provider. We will accept API keys for non-sensitive traffic in hosted route.
- Smart routing policy: SDK sets a traffic hint header (x-rw-sensitivity: low|high). The routing layer will forward \"low\" to hosted pool and \"high\" to Private pool inside Trela VPC. Fallback policy: if private capacity is saturated, we do graded degradation to smaller model in private or queue.

3) Embeddings & reranker
- Use an internal FAISS index for fast nearest-neighbor during POC. Periodic refresh job (nightly) to avoid drift.
- Reranker: two-stage pipeline — bi-encoder for candidates + cross-encoder fine-tuned on Trela labels for final rank. Store ranking model as a pinned artifact in our model catalog.

4) Structured output & tool-calling
- Use function-calling for schema-validated outputs where determinism matters (invoices, PII extraction). Implement JSON schema validation as a last-mile check before ingesting to Trela systems.

5) Prompt templates & governance
- Repo layout: /prompts/system/, /prompts/templates/, /prompts/redteam/ with semantic version tags.
- System prompts are immutable after release; each release gets a checksum and signed metadata. Deployments reference a prompt tag (e.g., system@v1.2).
- Red-team plan: 2 rounds — automated prompt-injection fuzzing followed by a manual review of high-risk templates. Results recorded in our eval dashboard.

6) Security / auditability
- Audit logs: token usage + prompt_tag + request_hash stored to customer-managed logs (Trela can forward to their SIEM).

I'll prepare a 15-min tech deck and demo code snippets for Thursday's deep dive. Any additions?

-Neha
Neha Kapoor
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference

Subject: Action items + MAP for Trela POC (see attached MAP + sample configs)

Alex —

Great — thanks for the quick turnaround and the attachments. Per our internal notes, attaching the Mutual Action Plan (mutual-action-plan-TRELA.xlsx) and the sample config. High-level action items I put into the MAP:

A. Trela (due 8/03 EOD): architecture diagram, security questionnaire (we have the partial PDF) — OWNER: J. Patel
B. Redwood (due 8/04): SDK quickstart, sample schema for structured output, red-team test plan — OWNER: Neha / Soojin
C. Both (target 8/10): provision POC env, deploy FAISS index + demo reranker, run initial eval suite — OWNER: Connor / Alex

Red-team & prompt injection note (specific ask from legal/security):
- We need permission to run prompt-injection probes against a staging subset of Trela data. Probes are non-destructive and will be run inside the POC environment only. We will provide a report and remediation suggestions.

Technical note on prompt versioning you asked about: we will publish a checksum for every system prompt release and include a simple CLI to verify a deployed prompt matches the checksum. Example flow:
1) developer references prompt tag system@v1.0 in SDK config
2) deployment records prompt_tag + checksum in audit log
3) if prompt file changes, checksum mismatch triggers an alert; older checksum remains accessible for audit.

Please confirm you are OK with the red-team probe and that J. Patel can create an OIDC test client for our client-credentials flow. If we get a quick \"ok\" from you, we'll lock the MAP and schedule the technical deep dive (30-45m) next week.

Connor
Connor O'Brien
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
